text: Traces capture model calls, retrieval, tool use, and custom logic so you can debug behavior and see where time is spent
quote: A trace captures model calls, retrieval, tool use, and custom logic so you can debug behavior and understand where time is spent.

text: Accepts traces over the OpenTelemetry protocol (OTLP), not tied to any specific LLM vendor or framework
quote: Phoenix offers comprehensive tracing capabilities that are not tied to any specific LLM vendor or framework. Phoenix accepts traces over the OpenTelemetry protocol (OTLP)

text: Auto-instrumentation for popular frameworks such as LlamaIndex, LangChain, DSPy, Mastra, and Vercel AI SDK
quote: Phoenix accepts traces over OpenTelemetry (OTLP) and provides auto-instrumentation for popular frameworks (LlamaIndex, LangChain, DSPy, Mastra, Vercel AI SDK)

text: Zero-config tracing: setting auto_instrument=True automatically traces AI libraries
quote: Zero-config tracing — Enable `auto_instrument=True` to automatically trace AI libraries

text: Tracing decorators such as @tracer.chain and @tracer.tool for manual instrumentation
quote: Tracing decorators — @tracer.chain, @tracer.tool, and more for manual instrumentation

text: A coding agent can set up tracing for your app by running the Phoenix CLI setup command
quote: Let your coding agent set up tracing for you: start Phoenix, then run `npx -y @arizeai/phoenix-cli setup` from your app's root directory.

text: Identify slow invocations of LLMs, retrievers, and other application components
quote: Application Latency: Identify and address slow invocations of LLMs, Retrievers, and other components within your application

text: Detailed token usage breakdown per LLM call to find the most expensive invocations
quote: Gain a detailed breakdown of token usage for your LLM calls, allowing you to identify and optimize the most expensive LLM invocations.

text: Inspect documents returned by retriever calls, including their scores and order
quote: Inspect the documents retrieved during a Retriever call, including the score and order in which they were returned

text: View the descriptions and function signatures of tools given to the LLM
quote: Tool Descriptions: View the descriptions and function signatures of the tools your LLM has been given access to

text: Organize traces into projects by environment, application, or team
quote: Projects: Organize traces by environment, application, or team

text: Group related traces into sessions to track multi-turn conversations
quote: Group related traces into conversations and user sessions

text: Query and analyze spans with filtering capabilities
quote: Spans — Query and analyze traces with powerful filtering capabilities

text: Deterministic code-based evaluators such as exact match, regex, and custom heuristics
quote: Phoenix supports both deterministic code-based evaluators (exact match, regex, custom heuristics) and LLM-as-a-judge evaluators

text: LLM-as-a-judge evaluators in which a second model scores output against a rubric
quote: Phoenix supports both deterministic code-based evaluators (exact match, regex, custom heuristics) and LLM-as-a-judge evaluators, where a second model scores the output against a rubric.

text: Configure evaluators in the UI and attach them to datasets; experiment results are scored automatically with no code
quote: Configure evaluators in the Phoenix UI and attach them to your datasets. Phoenix scores experiment results automatically — no code required.

text: Judge models are model-agnostic through adapters for OpenAI, LiteLLM, LangChain, AI SDK, and more
quote: Model Agnostic via adapters (for OpenAI, LiteLLM, LangChain, AI SDK, and more) — so you can easily switch judge models, or stick to your preferred provider.

text: LLM evaluations return explanations by default
quote: Built-in Explanations — all Phoenix LLM evaluations return explanations by default for better results and richer signals

text: Run thousands of evaluations without writing your own retry or concurrency logic
quote: This means you can run thousands of evaluations without writing any retry or concurrency logic yourself.

text: Every evaluation run records inputs, judge prompts, model reasoning, scores, and timing
quote: Every evaluation execution captures the input data, the exact prompts sent to the judge LLM, the model's full reasoning, the final scores, and execution timing.

text: Explore evaluation traces in the trace viewer to find systematic biases and improve evaluators
quote: Use Phoenix's trace viewer to explore evaluation traces, identify systematic biases, and continuously improve evaluator performance.

text: Run evaluations on production traces, experiment results, or any dataset
quote: You can run evaluations on traces from production, on experiment results, or on any dataset.

text: Score traces and spans with LLM evaluators, code checks, or human labels to track performance
quote: You can score traces & spans with LLM-based evaluators, code-based checks, or human labels so you can track performance and identify failures consistently.

text: Python and TypeScript SDKs for running evaluations against Phoenix traces, datasets, or any data source
quote: Python and TypeScript SDKs for running evaluations against Phoenix traces, datasets, or any data source. Full control over evaluation logic, judge models, and pipelines.

text: Attach ground-truth human annotation labels directly in the UI
quote: Attach ground truth labels directly in the UI

text: Prompt playground for trying prompts, models, and invocation parameters, with progress tracked through tracing and experiments
quote: Prompt Playground - Play with prompts, models, invocation parameters and track your progress via tracing and experiments

text: Compare prompt configurations and their responses in the playground
quote: Comparing prompt configurations and responses in the Phoenix playground

text: Span replay: step into a past LLM invocation and replay it with modifications to compare outcomes
quote: Span Replay - Replay the invocation of an LLM... you can step into the LLM invocation and see if any modifications to the invocation would have yielded a better outcome.

text: Prompt management to create, store, change, and deploy the prompts an application sends to LLMs
quote: Prompt Management: Create, store, change, and deploy the prompts that your application sends to LLMs.

text: Client SDKs keep prompts in sync across applications and environments
quote: Phoenix offers client SDKs to keep your prompts in sync across different applications and environments.

text: Version prompts and test prompt variants across datasets using real application examples before rollout
quote: Phoenix helps you iterate on prompts using real examples from your application. You can version prompts, test prompt variants across datasets, and replay calls to see how changes affect outputs before rolling them out.

text: Collect datasets from production, staging, evaluations, or manual entry for experiments and evaluations
quote: Datasets allow you to collect data from production, staging, evaluations, and even manually. The examples collected are used to run experiments and evaluations to track improvements to your prompt, LLM, or other parts of your LLM applicatio

text: Create versioned datasets of examples for experiments
quote: Datasets - Create versioned datasets of examples for experimen

text: Group traces into datasets, rerun them through different app versions, and compare evaluation results
quote: You can group traces into datasets, rerun them through different versions of your application, and compare evaluation results to confirm whether a change actually improved performance.

text: Dataset evaluators act as test cases that automatically score experiment outputs, like a unit test suite
quote: Dataset Evaluators serve as **test cases** that automatically score outputs when running experiments—forming an evaluation harness similar to a unit test suite.

text: Detect improvements or regressions, drill into good and bad examples, and compare examples against prior runs
quote: Understand whether an update is an improvement or a regression; Drill down into good / bad examples; Compare specific examples vs. prior runs

text: Free to self-host with no feature limits; data stays in your infrastructure and can be fully air-gapped
quote: Phoenix is **free to self-host** with no feature limitations. Your data stays entirely within your infrastructure—nothing is sent to Arize and can be fully air-gapped.

text: Deploy via CLI, Docker/Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, AWS CloudFormation, Railway, Render, Cloud Run, or Azure
quote: Terminal Run via CLI Docker Docker or Compose Kubernetes Deploy on K8s Helm Helm charts AWS CloudFormation Railway One-click template Render One-click blueprint Google Cloud Run One-click deploy Azure One-click ARM template

text: Start a local Phoenix server with a single command (uvx arize-phoenix serve)
quote: $ uvx arize-phoenix serve

text: Pin a specific Docker image version for production deployments
quote: Pin to a specific version (e.g., `arizephoenix/phoenix:version-8.0.0`) for production deployments.

text: Modular Python SDK packages, so you install only what you need
quote: Phoenix's Python SDK is modular by design, allowing you to install only what you need. Each package serves a specific purpose and can be used independently or together.

text: MCP endpoint lets MCP clients search, query, and operate on projects, traces, datasets, experiments, prompts, and annotations
quote: Point any MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, and others) at your Phoenix instance's `/mcp` endpoint and it can search, query, and operate on your projects, traces, datasets, experiments, prompts, and annotations

text: CLI command configures the MCP connection for agents such as Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and VS Code
quote: px setup mcp --agent claude   # or codex, gemini, cursor, opencode, vscode

text: Phoenix Intelligence, a built-in AI agent that inspects traces, iterates on prompts, and runs experiments
quote: Hand investigations to Phoenix Intelligence, the built-in AI agent that inspects traces, iterates prompts, and runs experiments

text: Built on OpenTelemetry and powered by OpenInference instrumentation
quote: Phoenix is built by Arize AI and the open-source community. It is built on top of OpenTelemetry and is powered by OpenInference instrumentation.
